title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Macalester spaces for studying, gathering, creating, performing, reflecting, and spending time outside class.

cards.title: Ruth Stricker Dayton Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Student-life hub
cards.notes: Use the CC as a central meeting point between classes; check its building-hours page and reserve a room ahead when planning a group gathering.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered campus hub with dining, lounges, rooms, and services.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes the Campus Center as a student-centered space and campus community hub with reservable spaces.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are listed as 7 a.m.–1 a.m. Monday–Friday and 10 a.m.–1 a.m. Saturday–Sunday; room use may require reservation.

cards.title: The Loch
cards.subtitle: Campus Center lower level
cards.notes: Bring a group for a low-key game or student event; the lower-level lounge has billiards tables and a performance-ready stage.
cards.short_summary: A lounge with billiards, dining during the academic year, and event infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester identifies The Loch as a student lounge with two billiards tables, a raised stage, and space for events including performances and trivia.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Campus Center lower level; use follows Campus Center building access and event arrangements.

cards.title: McPherson Atrium
cards.subtitle: Campus Center second level
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the second-floor lounge before a meeting or program, and keep the space flexible for other campus users.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor student lounge designed for gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester calls McPherson Atrium a student lounge area and a prime gathering space for students.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second level of the Campus Center; building hours and any event use are governed by Campus Center policies.

cards.title: John B. Davis Lecture Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Center lower level
cards.notes: Watch the college events calendar for a talk, screening, or performance held here; reserve it through campus processes for an approved event.
cards.short_summary: A 213-capacity venue for campus talks, films, and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists John B. Davis Lecture Hall as an event space for keynote speakers, film screenings, and performances, with capacity for 213.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Campus Center lower level; attendance and reservations depend on the particular program.

cards.title: DeWitt Wallace Library
cards.subtitle: 110 S. Macalester Street
cards.notes: Choose an individual room for focused work or one of the larger collaborative areas for a project; follow the library’s shared-space guidelines.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines individual study rooms with collaborative work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its spaces support studying, creating, and relaxing, from large open collaborative areas to individual study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours listed by the library are 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday–Thursday, with shorter Friday–Sunday hours; holiday and break hours vary.

cards.title: Idea Lab
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the available banner paper, markers, paint, and glue to make event materials; leave enough time for a student organization’s publicity plan.
cards.short_summary: A library maker space for student-organization posters and banners.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that the Idea Lab on the Library’s second floor provides paper, markers, paint, glue, and other supplies for student organizations’ promotional materials.
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s second floor; use supplies responsibly and confirm current availability with the library or student-life staff.

cards.title: Weyerhaeuser Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Center for Religious and Spiritual Life
cards.notes: Step in for a quiet period of reflection or study, and check the Center for Religious and Spiritual Life schedule before joining a program.
cards.short_summary: A campus reflection space that also hosts religious and spiritual-life programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s admissions guide identifies the Chapel as home to the Center for Religious and Spiritual Life and describes spaces for meditation, reflection, and quiet study.
cards.source_title: 102 Things to Do at Mac | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Check Center for Religious and Spiritual Life programming and building access before visiting; respect scheduled services and reflection use.

cards.title: The Great Lawn
cards.subtitle: Central campus green
cards.notes: On pleasant days, bring a book or meet a small group outdoors; leave room for classes, organized events, and others sharing the lawn.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor setting used for classes, informal gatherings, and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester reports that classes form circles on the Great Lawn and documents the annual fall Involvement Fair there.
cards.source_title: Our Campus Home: A Place of Belonging, A Window to the World | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space with weather-dependent use; organized programs may reserve portions of the lawn.

cards.title: Shaw Field
cards.subtitle: South campus athletic green
cards.notes: Use the open field only when it is not set for athletics or a campus program; check posted event information before starting a casual game.
cards.short_summary: A named campus field that appears in Macalester’s account of informal outdoor activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s campus-life article specifically describes people playing spikeball on Shaw Field.
cards.source_title: Our Campus Home: A Place of Belonging, A Window to the World | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather- and scheduling-dependent; yield to authorized athletic and campus events.

cards.entity_name: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center Gallery
cards.title: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Stop by to view student work, then use the comfortable seating for a short conversation or reset between classes while respecting exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A gallery with student exhibits and seating for casual gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s arts spaces page says the gallery provides exhibit space for student work and comfortable seating for casual gatherings.
cards.source_title: Studio and Rehearsal Spaces | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Exhibit access and any gallery events may vary; treat displayed work and seating as shared campus resources.
